Endpoint convolution norm equality is attained by the sign function, and the only nontrivial calculation is a finite consecutive cosine sum over the exactly identified negative interval. The finite verification is corroborative; the proof is valid for every integer \(N\ge3\).

value.rationale: The invariant is the endpoint norm of the first nontrivial consecutive-frequency Fourier projection on a finite cyclic group, a standard stability quantity rather than an arbitrary slice. The exact formula exposes a genuine \(N\bmod3\) sampling effect caused by whether the grid hits the zeros of the three-term Dirichlet kernel, and it gives the finite-to-continuous transition in closed form. This is a complete all-\(N\) classification of a natural discrete Lebesgue constant, not a numerical table or a routine parameter substitution.
